_meta.purpose: Cross-library interop for the crypto-core 4 hybrids, generated ONCE by hand and never by a script in the repo: noble signs and encapsulates here, OpenSSL (pyca/cryptography + backend/tests/xwing_ref.py) adds its half, and each side checks the other's. Keys are hex (identifiers), signatures, ciphertexts and secrets base64 (payloads), as on the wire.
_meta.patterned_keys: composite_secret_key is the bytes 00..3f and xwing_secret_key 40..5f, on purpose: test keys, not credentials.
_meta.ed25519_edges: Composite signatures with an honest ML-DSA half and a hand-built Ed25519 half carrying an order-2 component (in R, or in A with an odd or an even challenge k), plus a small-order A. noble strict accepts each Ed25519 half on its own; the clients refuse all four. OpenSSL refuses all but mixed_order_A_even_k, whose KEY the server refuses where it enters (security/ed25519_subgroup.py).
_meta.prime_order_points: The expected answer of "is this a canonical point of order exactly L", from noble (Point.fromBytes strict, !is0, isTorsionFree); the server computes the same in pure Python. No y below 19 is a point of order L (checked exhaustively when this was generated), so a non-canonical encoding (y + p) can never name one: the canonical-encoding rule and the subgroup rule agree on every input, and non_canonical here is refused by both.
